summary: All 49 validate_furigana failures are recoverable Layer-B defects in 7 lesson bodies; none needed a human and none required touching Layer-A Japanese (the visible text is byte-identical after every fix, and tag balance is preserved). Two shapes, as expected. (1) 32 spans with reading="": 22 of them annotate kana-only text (しまう, やってみる, を, やすい, にくい, づらい ...), where ruby carries no information and the empty attribute is a stray - those become the bare <jp> tag, which is the corpus-wide convention (5,629 kana-only bare <jp> spans in the lesson bodies versus 465 that repeat the kana in a reading attribute); the other 10 contain kanji and get a real reading rebuilt from corpus/vocab (使い, 読みにくいな, 読みにくい字, 言いづらい, 危険な, 使いにくい, 使いやすい, 説明しづらい, この放送は分かりやすい, 専門の質問は答えにくい). (2) 17 truncated readings: 13 in n4-aspecto-04 stop after the kanji reading and drop the okurigana tail (reading="た" over 食べてみて), and 4 are real transcription slips - 北だから lost its copula だ, 実際の畑仕事 was read じっさいに instead of じっさいの, 中止だ lost its だ, and 匂いがして was read がする. The durable source is research/derived/lessons/<slug>.json, not the DB: load_lessons.py re-authors every lesson from those files, so DB-only edits would be wiped. Every 'current' anchor is a byte-exact, unique substring of that file's body field (context prefixes added where the tag repeats, e.g. 書きなおす three times); applying all 49 and re-running the rule leaves 0 failures. Adjacent finding, out of this queue's scope because the rule only inspects spans containing hiragana: n4-aspecto-07 also carries <jp reading="">専門</jp> and <jp reading="">合</jp>, kanji-only spans whose ruby will never render. 専門 is せんもん; 合 standing alone as a component is ambiguous and would need an author.
